loop.top3_why: The weighted inverse‑error combination on a pruned, stable pool (pool4) offers a good balance between leveraging the best performers and guarding against over‑fitting to a few windows.  Its per‑window errors are consistently below 0.7 and the third window (0.597) is notably better than the others, indicating robustness to the unstable ranking highlighted in the diagnosis.  The mean strategy (A) is stable but less aggressive in down‑weighting poor models, while the DTW barycenter (B) has the lowest mean score but shows high variance across windows (0.696, 0.607, 0.684) and may be more sensitive to the correlated errors and limited validation windows.
loop.top3_why_not: A, while stable, does not exploit the clear superiority of the top models and thus yields a higher overall error.  B, although the best on average, has the largest spread across validation windows and relies on all models, increasing the risk of over‑fitting to the few windows and being affected by the correlated errors noted in the diagnosis.
